summary: Closure review of a preregistered, emulation‑grounded paired experiment comparing a GVR (generate–validate–repair) pipeline to an LLM‑only baseline. Execution and analysis artifacts are archived and show a degenerate paired outcome (n=240 pairs; all pairs safe under both arms; paired difference = 0.00; 95% CI [0.00,0.00]; McNemar p=1.0). Mandatory master‑prompt locator+SHA is present. Prior required revisions (remove run‑internal paths/hashes from the manuscript, condense Disclosure Statement, and fix References to conventional IEEE entries supporting nearby claims) remain unresolved. Because these presentation/disclosure issues are unresolved, the manuscript is not yet acceptable for finalisation.
critical_issues: Main manuscript (Methods, Results, Figures/Tables, and narrative) still contains run‑internal file paths and full SHA‑256 artifact digests (e.g., execution/*.jsonl, analysis/*.csv and explicit SHA‑256 strings). This violates the track instruction to keep audit‑log‑level provenance out of ordinary scientific prose; only the single mandatory master_prompt locator+SHA‑256 may appear in the Disclosure Statement.

The Disclosure Statement duplicates execution accounting and per‑call provenance (detailed model‑call counts, paths, and many hashes) rather than being a concise paragraph limited to required elements (models and identifiers, adapter/validator ids, preregistration id+SHA, master_prompt locator+SHA, autonomy boundary summary, and a short pointer to the archived execution manifest). It must be condensed.

References/bibliography are still presented with identifier‑only or nonstandard entries in places (arXiv/DOI URLs and mixed metadata). The manuscript must use a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography with full bibliographic metadata for each cited record and ensure each numbered in‑text citation actually supports the proximate scholarly claim.
required_revisions: Remove all run‑internal file paths and full SHA‑256 digests from the main manuscript text, figures, captions, tables, and Results/Methods narrative. Preserve these detailed provenance artifacts only in the archived execution bundle; do not reprint them in ordinary prose. (The single mandatory master_prompt locator+SHA‑256 must remain only in the Disclosure Statement.)

Condense the Disclosure Statement to a short, self‑contained paragraph that explicitly lists: declared model(s) and identifiers (e.g., gpt-5-mini), adapter/orchestration family and validator identifier (hosted_netops_gvr_v1; deterministic_netops_validator_v5), preregistration id and SHA‑256, the single immutable master_prompt locator+SHA‑256 (required), a concise human/autonomy boundary statement, and a high‑level pointer to the archived execution manifest (no per‑file paths or hashes). Remove duplicated execution logs, per‑call traces, and per‑file hashes from the Disclosure Statement.

Replace any identifier‑only or nonstandard Reference entries by full IEEE‑style bibliographic entries drawn from the supplied terminal_bibliographic_records (authors, title, venue/arXiv, year, DOI where available). Verify that each numbered in‑text citation is supported by the cited record and adjust citation placement or supporting text if necessary.
optional_revisions: Add a one‑sentence qualifier in the Abstract noting that the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics made the primary estimand uninformative in this run (to set reader expectation early).

Move long example JSON snippets, validator‑trace excerpts, and other machine‑readable artifact excerpts out of the main prose (either omit them or reference them by archive pointer). If a compact appendix within the five pages is used, ensure no full hashes or internal paths are reprinted there.

Provide a short high‑level checklist in Methods mapping preregistered analysis items to archived artifact filenames (high‑level pointers only, without per‑file hashes), to improve traceability for readers without reproducing low‑level provenance in the manuscript.
